rationale: Both produce comparable score tuples. A sorts the rank counts into a grouped list by (frequency, rank), which lets each category read its quad, trips, pairs and kickers straight from the grouped list. It checks the categories in standard poker order from straight flush down, with a small documented _is_straight helper, so correctness is easy to verify. B's named category constants are a real readability gain, but its checks run out of the natural order: flush before full house, straight after one pair. That is correct only through non-obvious reasoning about which combinations cannot coexist. It also repeats many next(...)/sorted(...) scans over counts. A has its own oddities, a needless tuple-unpack for the triplet kickers and a for-score-in-[...] trick in best_hands, but its overall structure is clearer and more straightforward.
